answer: The oasis report publishes the merge explicitly at each dune. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 58 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 150 times the capital for one share. The fee repeats 14 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
